Le Chatelier’s principle 
A system at equilibrium counteracts any change in the reaction conditions 
by shifting the equilibrium position (Le Chatelier’s principle). Changes in 
concentration, pressure or volume may affect the equilibrium position, 
although not the K value. The K value depends only on the temperature and 
the identity of reacting species (table 3). A catalyst increases the rates of the 
forward and reverse reactions equally, so it has no effect on the equilibrium 
position or the K value.

Reaction quotient 
The reaction quotient (Q) is calculated in the same way as the equilibrium 
constant (K) but from the concentrations of reacting species at a given point in 
the reaction instead of at equilibrium. The forward reaction is favoured when 
Q < K, while the reverse reaction is favoured when Q > K. If Q = K, the rates of 
both reactions are equal, so the system is at equilibrium.

Equilibrium calculations 
For reversible reactions, the position of equilibrium can be quantified by the 
equilibrium law. The K value depends only on temperature but not on other 
reaction conditions, such as pressure or concentrations. Therefore, it can be 
used to determine the composition of the reaction mixture at equilibrium.
